## Section 2: Borrower Overview and Relationship History

### Company Profile

Larkspur Precision Components, Inc. is privately held. [D5, ¶1] It was founded in 1994 in Rockford, Illinois, by Erik and Maria Halvorsen. [D5, ¶1] It makes precision-machined components and welded assemblies for agricultural and construction equipment OEMs. [D5, ¶1] It has about 310 employees and one plant. [D5, ¶1] The 2023 memo describes the same business from a single plant. [D3, Part B §2]

### Ownership and Management

Ownership is Erik Halvorsen 55%, Maria Halvorsen 25%, and Anders Halvorsen (COO) 20%. [D5, ¶1]

On the September 2, 2026 call, Erik Halvorsen (64) said he plans to hand the CEO role to Anders within three years. [D5, ¶5] On the same call, the family discussed "informally" selling a minority stake to a private equity firm. [D5, ¶5] There is no timeline and no LOI. [D5, ¶5]

### Relationship History

Larkspur has been a deposit and treasury management customer since 2019. [D5, ¶2] Average operating deposits were $4.1 million over the trailing 12 months to August 2026. [D5, ¶2] The Relationship Manager is P. Lindqvist. [D5, header]

A $12.0 million facility ($7.0M term loan, $5.0M revolver) was approved in June 2023. [D5, ¶2] The 2023 memo records the same $7.0 million term loan and $5.0 million revolving line of credit. [D3, Part B §1] The relationship has been paid as agreed with no past dues. [D5, ¶2]

The Q4 2024 compliance certificate arrived 18 days late. [D5, ¶3] Credit Administration waived the reporting covenant (waiver W-25-0117). [D5, ¶3] All later certificates arrived on time. [D5, ¶3] The FY2025 compliance certificate is dated April 28, 2026. [D1, §7]

### Current Request

On the August 19, 2026 call, Erik and Anders Halvorsen asked to increase the facility to $18.0 million. [D5, ¶4] The increase would fund a 60,000 sq ft expansion of the Rockford plant ($6.0 million), tied to a new multi-year Customer A program. [D5, ¶4] They want to close by November 30, 2026 so construction can start before winter. [D5, ¶4] They said a national bank has offered to deliver a term sheet within 10 business days. [D5, ¶4]

**Sources used:** D1 §7; D3 Part B §1 and §2; D5 header and ¶1-¶5.

**Underwriter to complete:**
- **Competing offer:** D5 ¶4 records the national bank offer only as a borrower statement. Not in provided documents: any term sheet or confirmation of the offer; the nCino notes or the borrower would normally hold it.
- **Management background:** Not in provided documents: biographies or tenure for Erik, Maria and Anders Halvorsen and any other senior management; the full credit file or management questionnaire would normally hold them.
- **Waiver W-25-0117:** Not in provided documents: the waiver document itself; Credit Administration records would normally hold it.
- **Change of control (legal review):** D2 §7.6 makes it an Event of Default if the Founders "cease to own, directly or indirectly, a meaningful portion of the voting equity interests of the Borrower, or cease to be actively involved in the management of the Borrower." [D2, §7.6] "Founders" means Erik Halvorsen and Maria Halvorsen. [D2, §1.1] "Meaningful portion" and "actively involved" are not defined in the excerpt. Refer both phrases to the underwriter and legal. Whether the CEO handover (D5 ¶5) or a minority stake sale (D5 ¶5) bears on §7.6 is for the underwriter and legal.
- **Customer concentration:** D4 §4.2.4 requires this to be addressed in Section 7 if any single customer exceeds 25% of revenue in the most recent fiscal year. D1 §5 reports Customer A at 31% of FY2025 revenue. The underwriter decides how to address it in Section 7.
- **Senior review:** D4 §4.2.3 sets senior review triggers, including total commitment above $15.0 million. The underwriter and Section 6 apply them.

Section 9 Risk Rating and Rationale: underwriter only, required.
